title: Implementation of Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan
body_text:
The Union Minister of Tribal Affairs Shri Jual Oram today laid a statement on the Table of the House that the Ministry of Tribal Affairs has reviewed the implementation of Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan on a continuous basis through periodic monitoring at the Ministry, State and district levels. The review has noted that Phase-I has established a nationwide community-based capacity-building framework for strengthening last-mile governance in tribal areas. The programme aims to create a cadre of trained government functionaries, community leaders, women’s collectives and tribal youth to facilitate responsive governance across approximately one lakh tribal villages in 30 States/UTs.
The programme has made significant progress towards developing transformative tribal leadership by creating a large cadre of trained grassroots leaders drawn from government institutions as well as tribal communities. The achievement made in developing transformative Tribal leadership through the abhiyan during phase 1 is as follow:
Approx. 15 lakh Adi Karmayogis mobilised through a cascading training architecture. More than 210 State Master Trainers, 2,200+ District Master Trainers and 11,000+ Block Master Trainers developed. 6,79,309 Adi Saathis and 4,03,306 Adi Sahyogis mobilised. 62,187 Tribal Village Vision 2030 Plans approved through Gram Sabhas. 54,324 Village Workbooks and 56,422 Adi Sewa Kendras (ASKs) recorded under the programme.
The Ministry has established an institutional mechanism to ensure continuity of capacity building, mentoring and follow-up support through Adi Sewa Kendras (ASKs) and Adi Karmayogi Volunteers (AKVs) .
The programme strengthens community leadership and participatory development by placing Gram Sabhas and tribal communities at the centre of local planning and implementation. During Phase-I, communities undertook household surveys, transect walks, focus group discussions and development-gap assessments, culminating in preparation of Tribal Village Vision 2030 documents and Village Action Plans covering health, education, livelihoods, housing, drinking water, connectivity, financial inclusion and social protection. Gram Sabhas formally approved these plans, thereby institutionalising participatory decision-making.
Under this mechanism, the following mechanism is contributing to strengthening community leadership and participatory development in tribal areas:
Adi Sewa Kendras (ASK) function as village-level single-window facilitation centres for information dissemination, entitlement facilitation, grievance redressal support and convergence with line departments. Adi Karmayogi Volunteers (AKV) , selected from local tribal youth, support day-to-day functioning of ASKs, assist citizens in accessing government schemes, documentation, grievance registration, Gram Sabha processes, awareness campaigns and periodic updating of village development priorities. Mapping of ASKs and registration of AKVs enables authenticated records, location-based monitoring and evidence-based strengthening of village institutions. Weekly monitoring by the Ministry, States and district administrations has been instituted to ensure effective implementation and sustainability of these village-level governance structures.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs informed Parliament that Phase-I of the Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan has built a nationwide capacity-building framework covering about one lakh tribal villages across 30 States/UTs. Key achievements include mobilising around 15 lakh Adi Karmayogis through a cascading training structure, approving 62,187 Tribal Village Vision 2030 Plans via Gram Sabhas, and establishing 56,422 Adi Sewa Kendras as village-level single-window facilitation centres supported by Adi Karmayogi Volunteers.
enrichment.context:
The Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan is a flagship capacity-building initiative under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs aimed at strengthening last-mile governance in tribal areas by creating a trained cadre of government functionaries, community leaders, women's collectives and tribal youth. It fits within the broader push for participatory, decentralized governance envisaged under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment and the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act (PESA), 1996, which empowers Gram Sabhas in Scheduled Areas to take a central role in local planning and resource management. By institutionalising Village Vision 2030 Plans and Village Action Plans covering health, education, livelihoods, housing, drinking water and financial inclusion, the programme seeks to operationalise the convergence of various tribal welfare schemes at the grassroots level.

The creation of Adi Sewa Kendras (ASKs) as single-window facilitation centres and Adi Karmayogi Volunteers (AKVs) as local youth facilitators reflects a broader trend in Indian governance towards community-driven service delivery models, similar to Common Service Centres and Gram Panchayat facilitation mechanisms. This initiative is significant for addressing historical governance deficits in tribal regions, improving last-mile delivery of entitlements, and building leadership capacity among Scheduled Tribes, which aligns with the Ministry's mandate under the Fifth and Sixth Schedules of the Constitution and various tribal empowerment programmes like the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN).

prelims_questions.question: With reference to the Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan, consider the following statements: 1. It aims to create a cadre of trained functionaries and tribal youth to strengthen governance in tribal villages. 2. Adi Sewa Kendras function as village-level single-window facilitation centres under the programme. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: Both statements are correct as per the release: the Abhiyan creates a cadre of trained functionaries and youth for governance, and Adi Sewa Kendras serve as single-window facilitation centres at the village level.

prelims_questions.question: The Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan, as reviewed by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, primarily focuses on strengthening governance in how many tribal villages across India?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states the programme aims to facilitate responsive governance across approximately one lakh tribal villages in 30 States/UTs.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of community-based capacity-building programmes like the Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan in strengthening last-mile governance in tribal areas. How do such initiatives complement the objectives of the PESA Act, 1996?
Examine the role of participatory institutions such as Gram Sabhas in tribal village planning, with reference to recent government initiatives for tribal development.

related_articles.relationship: PM-JUGA/DAJGUA is the overarching village saturation scheme under which the Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan's capacity-building framework and village-level planning (Vision 2030 Plans, Adi Sewa Kendras) operate, so this prior Parliament reply on PM-JUGA progress covers the same broader tribal village development initiative.
